chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibrahim ibn Abu al-Bilad, from Sadir who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

about the saying of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, our affair is difficult and exceedingly difficult, none approach it except a close angel, or a sent prophet, or a servant whose heart Allah has tested for faith.' He said: 'Because among the angels there are those who are close and those who are not, and among the prophets there are those who are sent and those who are not, and among the believers there are those whose hearts are tested and those who are not. So this affair of yours was presented to the angels, and only the close ones approached it; it was presented to the prophets, and only the sent ones approached it; it was presented to the believers, and only the tested ones approached it.' He said: 'Then he said to me: Pass through your hadith (i.e., continue/recount it).'

key_terms.أَمْرُنَا: Our affair (referring to the Imamate or divine authority)
key_terms.عَبْدٌ امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قَلْبَهُ: Servant whose heart Allah has tested

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the meaning of 'our affair is difficult' in the context of angels, prophets, and believers?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates Imam Ali’s (AS) description of the Imamate as 'difficult and exceedingly difficult' by employing a logical distinction between the general category and its specific elite subset. He clarifies that while all angels, prophets, and believers exist, only the *Muqarrabun* (those brought near), *Mursalun* (the sent ones with specific missions), and *Muhtanun* (those whose hearts God has tested for faith) possess the spiritual capacity to approach this station. This highlights the Shia concept of *Istidraj* and *Imtihan*, where divine authority is reserved for those who have undergone rigorous spiritual purification and testing.

en.basel-kadem: 82.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Muhammed, from Uthman bin Isa, from Saleh bin Maitham, from ‘Abaya al-Asadi, that he said: I heard the Commander of the Believers, peace be upon him, while he was sitting and I was standing:

I will surely come to Egypt to bring death, and I will surely come to demolish Damascus, stone by stone, and I will surely bring the Jews and the Christians out of all the nests of the Arabs, and I will surely drag the Arabs with this staff of mine. He said: I said to him: O Commander of the Believers, it is as if you are informing us that you will be revived after you die? He said: May such not be, O ‘Abaya. You thought into another direction of thoughts which a man from me knows. The compiler of this book, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Indeed, the Commander of the Believers, peace be upon him, used Taqiya with ‘Abaya al-Asadi in this narration, and he used Taqiya with Ibn al-Kawra’ in the previous narration, because they could not bear the secrets of the Family of Muhammed, peace be upon them.
